problem: Prior instruction-following agents on ALFRED rely on full subgoal supervision (about 20k instances) or expert trajectories, and fine-tuned LMs for subgoal prediction need lots of data. LM predictions are also poorly ranked (prompt-copying bias) and ignore environment state.
motivation: Language priors in LLMs encode object affordances and causal event structure, so they could plan subgoals from very few examples. Predicted plans must still be calibrated and grounded in what the agent observes in the environment before they can be executed.
key_idea: Prompt a frozen LM with a few (instruction, subgoal sequence) pairs to generate constrained top-k plans, re-score them with a mutual-information-style metric, then re-rank them with a small ranking model trained from environment execution feedback, and execute with a pre-trained low-level policy.
insight: Top-10 recall is much higher than top-1 (GPT-J 71% vs about 48%), so the LM proposes good plans but ranks them badly. Combining log p(h|τ) and log p(τ|h) with λ=1/2 gives consistently better top-1 recall than either alone. Environment-state re-ranking lifts ALFRED task success from 19.8 to 23.9, since state reveals which objects exist (e.g. a dining table vs a nonexistent side table). In-context learning beats fine-tuned T5-large at small N and has lower variance, but saturates and is limited by the 1024-token context.
method: Subgoal representation: a subgoal is (action, object) with 7 actions and 80 objects, verbalized as text like 'pick up apple'. Navigation subgoals are dropped, and sequences are comma-separated.

In-context subgoal generation: the prompt concatenates N 'instruction = subgoals' examples plus the query, using frozen GPT2-XL or GPT-J. Constrained beam search (beam 10) allows only tokens that keep a valid subgoal-sequence prefix.
Mutual-information re-ranking: hypotheses are scored by (1-λ) log p(h|τ) + λ log p(τ|h) with λ=0.5, where p(τ|h) comes from the LM prompted in the reverse direction (subgoals=instruction).

Environment-feedback ranking model: f = θᵀ concat(f_state(s), BERT_CLS(τ,g)), where f_state is the pooled and linearly projected HLSM voxel semantic map. It is trained with a softmax ranking loss on LM plans that succeeded when executed in AI2-THOR, using 1000 instructions.

Inference loop: generate top-k plans, execute the top-ranked plan's next subgoal with the HLSM low-level policy, prune plans inconsistent with executed subgoals, re-rank with the updated state, and stop at the stop subgoal (max 10 subgoals).
Low-level components: the HLSM pre-trained state estimation (segmentation/depth) and subgoal execution policy are used as-is.

setting.backbone: GPT-J 6B / GPT2-XL (frozen, in-context) + BERT ranking model (trained) + pre-trained HLSM low-level policy
setting.training_data: 22 in-context examples (2 per fine-grained task type) for subgoal generation; ranking model trained on execution feedback for 1000 ALFRED instructions; HLSM pre-trained models used as provided
setting.observation: egocentric RGB with estimated depth/segmentation, aggregated into an HLSM persistent voxel semantic map; high-level text instruction
setting.action_space: high-level subgoals (action, object) executed by the HLSM low-level policy (navigation + interaction)
setting.privileged: none for the predicted/re-ranked rows (oracle-subgoal row is an upper bound only)

numbers.backbone: GPT-J in-context + BERT ranking model + HLSM low-level policy
numbers.extra: ranking model trained with execution feedback on 1000 instructions; 22 in-context subgoal examples; only high-level instruction used

numbers.method: HLSM low-level policy + predicted subgoals (no re-ranking)
numbers.extra: top LM prediction without environment info; 22 in-context examples

numbers.method: HLSM low-level policy + oracle subgoals (upper bound)

numbers_note: Metrics use the paper's own names: SR = task success rate, GC = goal-condition success. Subgoal top-k recall (GPT-J top-1 47.80 and top-10 about 71% at N=22 on ALFRED val-seen) is not in the numbers list because ALFRED is not a canonical benchmark key for that metric. Some table cells in the source were CSV-loaded and not visible.
results: Combining in-context GPT-J subgoal prediction with feedback-based re-ranking reaches 23.9% task success on ALFRED val-seen, up from 19.8% without re-ranking. This beats MOCA (19.2) and Seq2seq (3.7) and is close to FiLM (24.6), but falls short of HLSM (29.6) and the oracle-subgoal bound (37.2). With only 11-33 examples, in-context GPT-J reaches 44-50% top-1 subgoal recall, beating GPT2-Medium fine-tuned on 779 instances (41.92) at just 11 examples, but full fine-tuning on 7793 instances is better (61.0).
limitations: Context length (1024 tokens) caps in-context examples at about 44, so performance saturates and fine-tuning wins when more data is available.
Navigation subgoals are dropped, the low-level policy is fixed and pre-trained, and high-level and low-level components are not learned jointly.
Task success is still below HLSM with full supervision, and errors come from ambiguous or noisy object annotations.
